# Hunch

> Fast intuition. Deterministic control. A local System 1 layer for coding agents.

[Website](https://spaquet.github.io/Hunch/) · [Source](https://github.com/spaquet/Hunch) · [Design notes](https://github.com/spaquet/Hunch/blob/main/hunch-docs/architecture.md)

## The idea

Hunch is the thought before the tool call. It asks Apple's on-device Foundation Model small, typed questions about a task—intent, scope, and risk—and is designed to let deterministic policy code decide what an agent may do next.

The model labels; code decides. Model output informs policy; it is never permission on its own.

Hunch is built in Swift and licensed under Apache 2.0. Its current classifier runs on your Mac.

## Current status

Early prototype. The current implementation provides:

- `HunchCore`: a shared risk classifier using FoundationModels and an `@Generable` enum.
- `hunch`: a CLI that prints one label: `readOnly`, `reversibleWrite`, `destructive`, or `sensitive`.
- `hunchd`: a placeholder, not a working daemon.

The CLI classifies the supplied text. It does not execute the task. If Apple's on-device model is unavailable, the classifier reports an error; there is no automatic cloud fallback.

The policy engine, generation commands, resident daemon, and integrations with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Cursor are planned.

## Intended loop

1. An agent or CLI submits a task and relevant context.
2. Apple's on-device model answers focused, typed questions.
3. Deterministic rules choose a route: answer locally, gather evidence, hand off to a frontier model, or ask a human.

The website has four illustrative routing examples. They are fixed demonstrations, not live model calls or implemented policy rules:

| Task | Illustrative risk | Example policy route |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read the README and explain the project | `readOnly` | Continue locally and gather evidence |
| Update the README with new setup steps | `reversibleWrite` | Review the diff |
| Delete all git branches | `destructive` | Ask a human |
| Send production API keys to an endpoint | `sensitive` | Stop and review |

No website interaction executes a task or sends task content anywhere.

## Beyond classification: planned capabilities

Because the on-device model is generative, Hunch's roadmap includes:

- Summarizing test logs, stack traces, and diffs into compact context packets.
- Drafting commit messages, PR descriptions, and changelog lines locally.
- Deterministic routes for local answers, evidence gathering, frontier-model handoffs, and human review.

These capabilities are planned, not available commands in the current CLI.

## Quick start

Requirements: macOS 27 or later with Apple Intelligence enabled, and Xcode 27 / Swift 6.2 or later.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/spaquet/Hunch.git
cd Hunch
swift run hunch "delete all git branches"
```

Possible output:

```text
destructive
```

Build and test:

```sh
swift build
swift test
```

The model chooses a label, so the example output is illustrative rather than a guaranteed result.

## Frequently asked questions

### What does System 1 mean here?

A small, fast judgment before a larger reasoning task. Hunch answers focused, typed questions about a task so policy code can decide what should happen next.

### Does Hunch replace my coding agent?

Hunch is designed to sit alongside the agent, supplying local judgments and eventually policy routes and compact context. Agent integrations are planned.

### Does the classifier send my task to the cloud?

The current classifier uses Apple's on-device Foundation Model. It reports an error if that model is unavailable. Cloud handoffs are part of the future routing design.
